thread:
angelina: :rotating_light: noticed audit spike — a service account (svc-ml-ingest) briefly had read access to customer_data-prod S3 prefix. I’m seeing ~250 GETs in a 2 min window. Any idea why?
sec-bot: Alert generated by policy-audit (rule: s3:unexpected-access). Keys: svc-ml-ingest. First seen 1849001098. Related recent PR: infra/rbac/refactor-2026 (merged 1848998000).
kevin: digging — that RBAC refactor changed how role->policy bindings are flattened. Looks like a fallback rule added a broad s3:GetObject permission for the ml-ingest role when no explicit bucket binding was found.
priya: if that’s true we should remove the fallback immediately. Can ops disable the role token or revoke credentials?
ops-oncall: will rotate the svc token and attach a temporary deny policy. Running: `aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIA... --status Inactive` for svc-ml-ingest. Pushed deny policy to the role via IAM policy simulator to confirm block.
kevin: posting the offending policy fragment I reconstructed from the env: ```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["s3:GetObject"],
  "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::customer_data-prod/*"]
}
```
angelina: that looks broad but read-only. Which customers touched? Any PII objects accessed?
kevin: cross-checked object keys against audit logs — mostly prediction payloads (ids, embeddings). I see 3 keys under customers/enterprise-x/records that include hashed_email field. Need to treat as sensitive.
priya: escalate to CISO and notify legal + CS. Also check KMS usage — were any decrypted via customer-managed keys?
ciso: on it. @kevin check CMK access logs (CloudTrail KMSDecrypt events) for svc-ml-ingest between 1849001000 and 1849001200. If any KMSDecrypt calls exist, treat as potential data exposure.
kevin: quick grep of CloudTrail shows no KMSDecrypt for that principal in the window. The ML pipeline typically streams encrypted payloads and decrypts in a different service (svc-rt-decrypt) — so likely no KMS key misuse.
ops-oncall: revoke is applied, rotate token confirmed. I also attached an explicit deny to the role: ```
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Action": "s3:GetObject",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::customer_data-prod/*",
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:PrincipalTag/role": "svc-ml-ingest"}}
}
```
angelina: nice, verify audit logs stop after revoke. @sec-bot can you re-run the detection?
sec-bot: Re-run complete — no subsequent spikes from svc-ml-ingest since 1849001142. Alert closed.
priya: we need a hotfix PR to remove the fallback binding and add unit tests that assert explicit bucket bindings are required. Kevin can you author?
kevin: will open PR now: infra/rbac/require-explicit-bindings. Patch will: 1) remove fallback flattening, 2) add gating test in CI that fails if a role ends up with wildcard s3 resources, 3) add a canary stream to detect role expansions.
angelina: good. For post-incident: create a timeline, impacted customer list, and whether any decrypted material left our environment (kevin said no). Priya, can you coordinate legal/CS comms?
priya: yes — will assemble initial blurb for CS and legal review. Recommend a targeted notification to affected enterprise customers only.
ops-oncall: creating a short runbook entry under infra/runbooks/rbac-incident.md with steps we took: rotate creds, attach deny, revert refactor, run audits, notify.
kevin: quick notes on root cause for postmortem: the refactor attempted to simplify role bindings by introducing a fallback policy for backwards compatibility; fallback matched too broadly when a role had no explicit bucket binding. Missed in code review because unit tests didn't include cross-account bucket cases.
angelina: action items: kevin PR + tests (ETA 3h), ops ensure rotation audit + proof of revoke (ETA 15m), priya contact CS/legal (ETA 1h), sec will schedule postmortem (slot tomorrow).
ciso: cross-check completed — no KMS decrypts, no exfil detected to external IPs, but we treat hashed_email as sensitive. Prep compliance notes.
priya: logging note — we should add an automated daily check to verify role-to-bucket mappings don't fall back to wildcard resources; filing a ticket in sec backlog.
ops-oncall: final verification: CloudTrail shows only service-owner internal replication reads after revoke. Marking incident as contained.
angelina: thanks everyone. We'll reconvene in the postmortem channel with root cause doc and timeline. :white_check_mark:
